analysis: The trial executed successfully but did not improve validation macro HR@10: 0.5000 versus the preceding 0.5037 and baseline 0.5050, decreases of 0.0037 and 0.0050. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.545, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.540, Electronics 0.390, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.525. Electronics increased from the reported preceding 0.380 to 0.390, but aggregate performance declined. Uniform transition weighting therefore did not support the proposed improvement in this run; these results do not establish that recency weighting is generally superior. The change preserved per-history normalization, so eligible histories retained equal aggregate influence. Host-reported allocated GPU time was 527.18 seconds.
code_summary: Trained one independent SASRec model per category from scratch with seed 42, selecting and loading exactly one validation-selected checkpoint per category. Each model uses 96-dimensional item and positional embeddings, two causal Transformer blocks with two attention heads, dropout 0.2, and a jointly trained causal history-attention pool blended through a learned gate. Scores use normalized embeddings, a learned scale, and jointly trained item biases. The isolated change assigns uniform weights to up to 24 randomly selected valid transitions per history, preserving sampled-softmax cross-entropy with 256 negatives, training-history exclusion masks, and float32 per-history scatter reductions. Prefix augmentation, AdamW, learning-rate schedule, stopping, dataset routing, and predictor writer remain unchanged. No ensembles or separately fitted scoring components are used.
